questions.question: 1. What is the Space Complexity of Topological Sorting?( N= number of vertices , E = number of edges)

explanations.a: Incorrect. O(N+E) represents time complexity, not space complexity.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(N) alone doesn't account for all the space requirements.
explanations.c: Correct. While enqueuing a node, we need some extra space to store temporary values. Other than that, the ordering can be done in-place. Hence space complexity is O(|V|) using DFS.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(V*E) is too large for the space complexity of topological sorting.

questions.question: 2. What is the most efficient Time Complexity of Topological Sorting?( N= number of vertices , E = number of edges)

explanations.a: Correct. The most efficient time complexity of Topological Sorting is O(N+E), where N is the number of vertices and E is the number of edges, as we visit each vertex and edge once.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(N) doesn't account for processing all the edges in the graph.
explanations.c: Incorrect. O(V) is the same as O(N) and doesn't account for edge processing.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(V*E) would be much slower than the actual efficient complexity of topological sorting.
